title: Review shared core primitives and root-level contracts in src/shared
scope: Primary ownership for root-level src/shared helpers and root contracts assigned to #410 in the shared-module ledger.

summary.overallAssessment: The root shared surface is mostly useful, but it is still carrying too many neighboring responsibilities in a few high-consumer files. The biggest remaining cleanup opportunities are env/runtime policy composition, numeric normalization overlap, keeping the new helper leaf splits from collapsing back into broad buckets, and continuing the metrics and ops family deflation work.

clusterFindings.assessment: This is still the weakest root-level cluster. The facades are slimmer now, runtime-envelope.js and auto-policy.js root facades have been removed, and env.js remains the main broad family that needs to keep its leaf splits stable instead of regrowing monolithic behavior.

These helpers are individually useful, but limits.js and number-coerce.js overlap enough to create duplicate entry points for the same coercion decisions. sort.js and order.js are fine together, but their boundary should stay explicit. path-normalize.js is coherent and should remain the canonical repo-relative and platform path layer.

metrics/core.js and observability.js have a healthy conceptual split, but the metric registry family still needs to resist becoming a new monolith. The ops helpers are finally under an explicit family path; the remaining work is keeping them there and not reintroducing flat root-level operational helpers.

The recent hard cutovers created several good narrow shared helpers. The important follow-up is to keep these leaf modules explicit and prevent them from being absorbed back into broad root utility buckets.

highestPriorityFollowUps.reason: The file is the de facto env registry for runtime, testing, bench, extractor stubs, TUI, and misc feature flags. Its size and consumer count make boundary drift likely.
The root facade is gone; keep resolution, current-process derivation, env patching, and parsing in the runtime-envelope leaf modules instead of recreating a broad facade.
The root auto-policy facade has been removed; keep policy assembly, repo scanning, and profile selection in the existing narrow auto-policy leaves.
The split happened, but the registry core still needs to stay narrow while additional metric families are pushed into dedicated leaves.
Its API surface overlaps heavily with number-coerce.js. One module should become the canonical numeric-normalization entry point.
New narrow shared helpers like search-request.js and repo-paths.js should stay explicit and should not be reabsorbed into broad root utility modules.
